messages:
incident-bot: ALERT P2: increased runtime latency & kernel-fallback events in canary after recent rollout. p95 x4, kernel_fallback_rate spiking. paging @sylvia
sylvia: oncall acked, what's the rollout id / flag?
matt: that's rollout `slice-batcher-rollout-19` (flag: slice_batching_v3), started 2024-06-21T11:02:00Z, at 6% canary
nisha: seeing fallback to slow_kernel on canary hosts, sample log: 
```
2024-06-21T11:07:12Z runtime WARN kernel_select: fallback_path=slow_kernel model=tulu-13b quant=8bit batch_window=80ms
2024-06-21T11:07:20Z metrics p95=520ms p99=1.6s
```
nisha: note batch_window was increased from 25ms -> 80ms in this rollout config
ashok: I can toggle LD flag to stop traffic. want me to kill the rollout?
matt: yes, flip to off for canary and pause auto-scaling. initiating rollback of the rollout config
ashok: flag toggled OFF for canary audiences :white_check_mark:
cust-ops-bot: customer-impact: two customers reported elevated latencies and a few 504s between 11:07-11:18 UTC. Tickets: C-1304, C-1305. CS notified.
ryan: propose mitigation: 1) LD off (done) 2) rollback batch_window change (matt) 3) limit canary RPS to 0.4 per host (ryan) 4) enable kernel_affinity=legacy on effected hosts (sylvia)
sylvia: agreed. will flip kernel_affinity and add a temporary route policy
matt: rollback PR opened and applying revert now, will patch canary slices (https://git.internal/r/rollouts/pull/459)
nisha: quick grep shows KV eviction spikes aligning with fallback events: `grep -n "kv_eviction" /var/log/runtime/canary-*.log | sed -n '1,5p'`
ashok: LD confirms no traffic for canary audience.
incident-bot: ROLLBACK job started 11:15 UTC for revert `pull/459`
ryan: applied rate limit policy to canary routes (max_rps=0.4) in region-us-east1
matt: rollback finished on 10/11 canary hosts, node-4 failed to restart and is in provisioning loop
sylvia: p95 dropping back toward baseline on healthy nodes. checking node-4 logs for OOM / stuck prefetch
matt: node-4 logs show repeated `madvise` fallback warnings and a hung prefetch thread. restarting runtime service now
nisha: after restart, KV eviction counters normalized and kernel fallback events went back down. overall p95 ~ baseline
cust-ops-bot: CS updated: customers C-1304/C-1305 notified with root-cause and mitigation steps. no SLA breach expected, monitoring continues
ryan: please create an incident page and assign RCA owners. suggest owners: nisha (metric analysis), matt (deployment pipeline fix), ashok (flag gating)
sylvia: follow-ups: 1) revert batch_window change in main rollout until perf harness validated 2) add an alert for kernel_fallback_rate and kv_eviction_rate 3) add pre-deploy perf smoke that checks KV eviction and p95
matt: will enforce a rollout gate in the pipeline to block batch_window increases >2x without smoke passing
nisha: hypothesis: large batch_window changed batching patterns, increasing effective sequence footprints hitting a kernel path that is slower for some memory layouts -> kernel fallback + KV churn. need reproducible test with emulated batching patterns
ashok: adding a LaunchDarkly rule requiring `perf_smoke_passed=true` before scaling past 5%
sylvia: lowering severity to P3 at 11:40 UTC. moving to post-incident review and handing off to daytime SREs
incident-bot: INCIDENT update: severity=P3, status=mitigated, timeline: https://confluence.internal/incidents/1747004321
sylvia: closing live coordination thread. please add timeline notes and tag owners for RCA. :slightly_smiling_face:
